As we wrap up, let's bring everything together and talk about what these ideas really mean for you as a leader, day to day.
Becoming a great manager isn't about following some rigid playbook—it's about questioning old habits, and zeroing in on what truly matters: the unique strengths and talents of each person on your team.
So, how do you actually put this into practice?
First, focus on strengths—not just resumes or experience—when you're building your team. Make it your priority to define clear outcomes, then trust people to find their own way there. Have regular, one-on-one coaching conversations that put each person’s growth and engagement front and center.
Build teams that celebrate a mix of strengths, and don’t get stuck trying to fix every weakness. Keep high performance going with real recognition, ongoing development, and a shared sense of purpose.
And remember—being a great manager doesn't mean having all the answers or controlling every little thing. It’s about creating the space where people can truly shine, where they feel seen, trusted, and inspired to push themselves just a little further.
Sure, there’ll be bumps in the road, moments when things don’t go as planned. That’s just part of the journey. What really matters is your commitment to learning and your genuine care for your team. Every conversation, every small adjustment, every time you recognize someone—it all adds up. By focusing on strengths and building real relationships, you’ll help your team achieve more than you ever imagined. And you’ll find more meaning and satisfaction in your own work as a manager, too.
So as you move forward, remember: leadership’s a journey best traveled with empathy, openness, and a steady belief in the potential of those around you.
